data.title: Ceftriaxone
data.body:
_Injectables · III Antibiotics_

**Class:** Third-generation cephalosporin (β-lactam)

## Mechanism of action
- Binds penicillin-binding proteins and inhibits cell-wall synthesis → bactericidal
- Stable against many β-lactamases; good Gram-negative cover (Neisseria, Haemophilus ducreyi, Enterobacteriaceae) with streptococcal cover

## Pharmacokinetics
- IM or IV; long half-life (6–9 h) → once-daily dosing
- Good CSF penetration with inflamed meninges
- Dual excretion (bile ~40% and urine) — no dose change in renal failure alone

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Gonorrhoea (uncomplicated: urethral, cervical, rectal, pharyngeal) and disseminated gonococcal infection
- Chancroid; PID (with doxycycline + metronidazole)
- Neurosyphilis (alternative when penicillin cannot be used); early syphilis alternative
- Lyme disease (late/neurological), cellulitis, severe skin and soft-tissue infections, meningococcaemia, typhoid

## Dose & formulations
- Uncomplicated gonorrhoea: 500 mg IM single dose (1 g if over 150 kg) — CDC 2020; some guidelines (WHO 2024) use 1 g IM
- Chancroid: 250 mg IM single dose
- Disseminated gonococcal infection: 1 g IV/IM daily
- Neurosyphilis (alternative): 1–2 g IV/IM daily × 10–14 days
- Skin infections: 1–2 g IV daily
- Reconstitute IM dose with 1% lignocaine to reduce pain (never give lignocaine-mixed solution IV)

## Adverse effects
- Injection-site pain, phlebitis
- Hypersensitivity (rash, urticaria, anaphylaxis); cross-reactivity with penicillin is low (about 1–2%)
- Diarrhoea, C. difficile colitis
- Biliary pseudolithiasis (reversible sludge), especially in children with high doses
- Immune haemolytic anaemia (rare); SJS/TEN (rare)

## Contraindications
- Severe immediate hypersensitivity (anaphylaxis) to penicillins or cephalosporins
- Neonates with hyperbilirubinaemia (displaces bilirubin → kernicterus)
- Neonates receiving IV calcium-containing solutions (fatal calcium–ceftriaxone precipitates)

## Drug interactions
- Calcium-containing IV fluids (Ringer lactate) — do not mix in the same line
- Warfarin effect may increase

## Monitoring
- Test of cure for pharyngeal gonorrhoea (7–14 days); test for HIV, syphilis and chlamydia; treat partners

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe in pregnancy (old FDA category B) — the gonorrhoea treatment of choice in pregnancy.

## Viva points
- Drug of choice for gonorrhoea (single IM dose)
- Dual excretion — no renal dose adjustment
- Calcium precipitate risk in neonates
- Biliary sludge (pseudolithiasis)

## Note on sources
Gonorrhoea dose differs between guidelines (CDC 500 mg, older guidelines 250 mg, WHO 2024 1 g). Please use whatever dose your department or NACO follows.

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.9; Khopkar ch.1; CDC STI Treatment Guidelines 2021. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
